title: Runtime Evolution Guardian and Migration Orchestration Policy
creator: Ava Chen
description: Purpose: establish a single, operational policy (the 'Guardian') that governs runtime semantic versioning, LTS channels, automated rollout gates, and the migration orchestration tooling (the 'Migration Orchestra'). Scope: serving runtime API and runtime-side client adapters used by hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Goals: minimize user-facing regressions during evolution, guarantee clear deprecation windows, enable safe automated rollouts with telemetry-driven gates, and ship CLI/console tooling that makes upgrades low-friction for customers and internal teams.
acceptance_criteria: A semver classification table (major/minor/patch) with concrete examples for runtime behavior is published and linked in the public runtime-1.20 release notes
An LTS channel definition exists: LTS (18 months + 6 month security-only), Stable (rolling monthly), Canary (nightly), and is wired into Console release selector
Rollout gate automation implemented: canary -> graduated % increases -> auto-rollback on gate failure
Migration Orchestra CLI (ri-upgrade) prototype that performs dry-run compatibility checks and generates migration hints is merged behind feature flag
Deprecation header protocol (X-RI-Deprecation, X-RI-Replacement-Version) implemented in runtime responses and surfaced in Console
Rollback playbook documented with exact metric thresholds and runbooks linked in attachments
decisions: Adopt semantic versioning where MAJOR denotes incompatible API/behavior changes, MINOR denotes additive but potentially opt-in features, PATCH is bugfix/backwards compatible changes
Introduce a runtime-only 'compatibility signal' header (X-RI-Compat) that allows clients to opt into compatibility shim behavior during transition windows
LTS will only accept PATCH and security MINORs; MAJOR bumps require a coordinated non-LTS migration track
Deprecation windows: Stable features get 60 days notice before removal; LTS features get 180 days with security-only extension available for customers under contract
We will gate all MAJOR and MINOR rollouts with automated telemetry checks before increasing traffic beyond canary traffic slices
rollout_gates: Canary slice: 0.5% traffic for 6 hours, then 1% for 24h if green
Gate criteria to be evaluated automatically every 10 minutes: error-rate delta < 0.3% absolute, p99 latency regression < 7%, token-per-request CPU < 12% change
Quality gate: downstream eval set (prompt suite) must show no Rouge/semantic drift above defined thresholds; automated NLU checks must pass
Operational gate: no new client-side exceptions in telemetry for 24h window (exceptions defined by 'runtime-unhandled' events)
If any gate fails, system will: (1) stop rollout, (2) shift canary traffic to previous variant, (3) create alert to on-call, (4) open rollback PR if automated rollback fails
deprecation_policy: Runtime must emit deprecation headers: X-RI-Deprecation: 2025-06-01, X-RI-Replacement-Version: 1.20.3
Console will surface deprecations to customers with per-token cost/feature usage impact and suggested migration steps
Soft-deprecations: for additive API toggles we will use 'soft-deprecate' with opt-in flag for two cycles before hard removal
Removal windows: for Stable features minimum 60 days; for LTS features minimum 180 days plus security extension option; emergency removals require Exec sign-off and targeted customer notifications
Clients should implement X-RI-Compat negotiation and accept a 'compat-shim' response header to receive temporary compatibility behavior
upgrade_tooling_tasks: ri-upgrade CLI: dry-run mode that hits /compat-check with --api-key and produces a compatibility report (examples in attachments)
Console migration panel: per-customer 'upgrade readiness' page showing model/runtime compatibility score and recommended config changes
Automated PR generator: given a deprecation, generate suggested client library changes and an example changelog entry in GitHub
Rolling upgrade operator: server-side controller that increments traffic slices and evaluates gates per rollout_gates thresholds
Migration assistant: a guided checklist (in-Console) that creates a canary plan, auto-enables compatibility headers for a limited window, and schedules reminders
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit compat_probe events for every ri-upgrade dry-run with schema {client_id, route, server_version, compat_score}
Track runtime.response.deprecation_warning with count by variant, route, and customer_id
Produce a daily compatibility-report artifact and store in infra S3 path referenced in attachments
Add p95/p99 latency, error-rate, token-CPU, and semantic-drift metric series tagged with rollout_id for automated gate evaluation
Collect client-negotiation headers (X-RI-Compat) and record shim-usage rates
migration_playbook: Step 0: Announcement - prepare deprecation email, doc page, and console banner (owner: PM)
Step 1: Compatibility audit - run ri-upgrade across top 100 customers, produce action items (owner: Solutions Eng)
Step 2: Canary - create a rolling plan using Migration Orchestra, start at 0.5% per rollout_gates
Step 3: Scale - if gates green, advance increments (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%), monitor tied metrics
Step 4: Finalize - remove compatibility shim after deprecation window and update docs and SDK changelogs
Rollback: automatically revert to previous runtime artifact and open incident communication channel; run hotfix patch if cause isolated to new code path
comments: 2025-02-12 Ava Chen: Drafted initial policy; focused on producing a single source of truth for deprecation windows and rollout gates. Filed as P0 to get cross-functional review.

notes: We intentionally separate LTS and Stable tracks to reduce upgrade panic. LTS customers will get a more conservative cadence and an explicit security-only extension path.
Consider future work: automated client-side adapter releases coordinated with runtime releases (owner: SDK team).
Follow-on ticket needed to implement per-route latency tiers and integrate them into rollout_gates (suggest ENG-90212).
